chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sukuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who bequeaths a share of his wealth.

He said: The share is one of eight, due to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The charities are only for the poor, the needy, those who work upon (acquiring) them, those with affectionate hearts, the necks (of human beings in captivity to be liberated), those in debt, for the sake of Allah and for the stranded traveler.'

key_terms.وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ: And those whose hearts are to be reconciled
key_terms.وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: And in the cause of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a 'share' in Islamic bequests according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defining the unspecified term 'sahm' in bequests as one of eight, deriving this from the eight categories of Zakat recipients in Surah al-Tawbah. This ruling illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of using Quranic structural divisions to interpret legal terminology in hadith, ensuring that bequests align with the divine distribution model. It highlights the continuity between Zakat obligations and voluntary bequests in Shia fiqh.
